founding_year.basis: founded 2003 by Fred Wilson and Brad Burnham (Wikipedia infobox and lead); the firm's own About page dates its first fund, USV 2004 ($125M), to 2004 — the fund year, not the firm's

history.value: Union Square Ventures was founded in New York in 2003 by Fred Wilson and Brad Burnham, with a $125M first fund. It was an early backer of Twitter, Etsy, Tumblr, MongoDB, Twilio, Duolingo and Coinbase, and one of the first institutional investors in crypto. Its core funds are now $275M each, alongside a climate fund family started in 2021.
history.basis: composed from the run's verified facts: founders and 2003 (Wikipedia), the $125M 2004 fund and the $275M core funds (usv.com/about), entry rounds from the firm's own announcement posts on the confirmed base (Etsy 2006, Twitter 2007, Tumblr 2007, Zynga 2008, 10gen 2008, Kickstarter 2009, Twilio 2009, Duolingo 2011, Coinbase 2013, Cloudflare 2012), the Opportunity Fund's 2010 Form D, the Climate funds' 2020-2022 Form Ds, the partner list from the live people page, the ADV roster (26 funds, $3,235,446,464 gross) and the landed base's own counts. Rewritten to the reader-facing shape (PRO-147, 2026-09-24). The Opportunity Fund (2010) and its later rounds (Cloudflare, Lending Club, Stash, Justworks), the current partners and the fund count are in the basis above. The old thesis was the firm's own sentence, kept in substance.

investment_concept.value: “We invest at the edge of large markets being transformed by technological and societal pressures.”
investment_concept.basis: The firm's own statement, verbatim from its meta description, second sentence (the first is 'Union Square Ventures is a venture capital firm based in New York City.'); the same sentence opens usv.com/about, read 2026-09-26; sentence case, straight quotes and a closing period are the only edits. PRO-147: the thesis is the firm's own crisp statement (Erik, 2026-09-26). Published inside quotation marks, as the firm's own words (Erik, 2026-09-26).

investment_stage.basis: the About page names the Core and Climate funds as 'early-stage, Seed & A' and the Opportunity Fund as 'later-stage'; the landed 220-row base reads Seed 73 / Series A 111 / Growth 35 / Pre-Seed 1 (Growth = Series B+ incl. the Opportunity Fund's later rounds and two secondary entries). Pre-Seed omitted at one row

investment_geo.basis: DERIVED, no site filters exist: hq_country on the 220-row base is US 177 / GB 11 / DE 10 / CA 6 / BR 2 / IN 2 / AU 2 and one each of CO, SE, NO, EE, FR, MX, EG, CH, IE, FI; the firm's one office is New York (ADV Item 1.F; 66 of 220 HQs are New York) — a US core with European, Canadian and Latin American positions, none marketed as a territory

investment_scope.basis: focus from the firm's own site sector tags on 347 base rows, crosswalked to data/taxonomy/focus.json (crosswalk in config.json), published above 10 companies. Scope type is the curated judgement carried in investor.json.

investment_range.basis: Median: entry-round amount sold on the first priced Form D of 67 membership-verified base companies with filing histories: p25 $2.33M, median $5.0M, p75 $11.3M, published as $5M — a round-size proxy for check size, fair where the firm led (it leads most Seed and A rounds it announces). Lower limit: the documented smallest institutional entry, Tumblr's $750K seed with Spark Capital (October 2007, the firm's own post); the $50K Clickable filing is a partial sale, not an entry check. Upper limit: the largest rounds the firm led out of the Opportunity Fund, Cloudflare's $50M Series C (2012) and Justworks' $50M Series E (2020, co-led); larger participations (Twitter's 2009 $98M round, Etsy's $40M 2012 round) were not USV-led

notable_investments.basis: The five best known of the firm's own companies, most recognised first: the names a general reader would recognise first (PRO-152, Erik 2026-09-24). Each is tied to its portfolio row by `slugs`; names read as a reader knows them, without legal suffixes (COLLECTION.md §8). Previously listed (10): Twitter, Etsy, Tumblr, Coinbase, Twilio, Duolingo, Cloudflare, Kickstarter, Zynga, MongoDB.

aum.basis: Union Square Ventures, LLC is an exempt reporting adviser (SEC 802-75126, venture capital fund adviser exemption), so no Item 5.F regulatory AUM exists; the sworn substitute is Schedule D Section 7.B.(1): 26 private funds with gross asset values summing to $3,235,446,464 (annual amendment filed 2026-03-27, parsed at run time, scratch/adv-7b-funds.json, first-appearance sequences of 26 names, 805- identifiers and values). Both range ends are that one number. No press figure is higher: the firm publishes fund sizes, not AUM

sources.note: the firm's own About page: the original early-stage fund (2004) was $125M; predates electronic Form D. Listed in the ADV 7.B roster only through its successors (the 2004 vehicle is fully realized).
